What slows real estate teams down

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

  • Portal and ad leads go cold before anyone calls back

    Enquiries from 99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com, Meta and Google arrive around the clock into separate dashboards and inboxes. The same buyer appears from several sources, nobody owns the first call, and by the time someone rings back the buyer has already spoken to another project.

  • Channel partner claims turn into disputes

    Brokers register the same customer, direct enquirers walk in after a partner's visit, and brokerage depends on spreadsheets and memory. Each dispute costs partner trust and delays payouts, and partners hold back their best clients.

  • Bookings, demands and loans run on paper chases

    KYC copies, allotment letters, agreement drafts, bank sanctions and milestone demand letters move between sales, CRM, legal, finance and lender relationship managers by email and paper. An error in a demand letter or a missed disbursement request hurts both cash flow and buyer confidence.

  • Buyers feel in the dark until possession

    Progress updates are irregular and do not always match what the developer files with the RERA authority. Possession appointments, final dues questions and snag complaints are handled on calls, and defect reports after handover go missing.

  • Site information arrives late and in pieces

    Daily progress sits in WhatsApp groups, labor counts on paper and material requests in phone calls. Project managers and clients see slippage days late, subcontractor bills cannot be checked against attendance, and near misses are never recorded.

  • Regulation touches every message and site

    RERA details in every advertisement, DPDP consent and security duties, TRAI rules for calls and SMS, PMLA duties for brokerages above the turnover threshold and labor code obligations on site all apply at once. Personal phones and spreadsheets cannot show what was sent, approved or consented to.

Every enquiry answered, qualified and walked to a site visit

One lead engine connects portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website, missed-call numbers and channel partner registrations to your CRM. Each enquiry is deduplicated and attributed, answered promptly with approved project content and the RERA registration number on a channel the buyer agreed to, qualified, assigned with response-time alerts and taken through visit booking, reminders, check-in and follow-up.

What changes

  • Faster first contact on portal and ad leads, including evenings and weekends
  • Fewer duplicate leads and attribution disputes between sources and partners
  • More visits kept, because confirming or rescheduling takes one tap
  • Clear evidence of which sources, campaigns and partners produce visits and bookings
  1. 1

    Capture and deduplicate every source

    Portal leads by API or export, depending on each portal package, plus ad lead forms, website forms, missed calls and partner registrations reach the CRM within minutes and are matched by phone, email and portal lead ID, so each buyer has one record with every source kept for attribution.

    nn8nZCZoho CRMSSupabase
  2. 2

    Reply within minutes, with consent

    Opted-in leads receive an approved WhatsApp template with the brochure, RERA registration number and next steps; others are called by the assigned executive within TRAI's seven-day enquiry window and offered the opt-in. Questions are answered only from the approved project knowledge base.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformACAnthropic ClaudeQQdrant
  3. 3

    Qualify and assign with alerts

    A short WhatsApp Flow or call script records configuration, budget band, timeline, home-loan need and resident or NRI status. Rules set by the sales head score and assign the lead, and the sales manager is alerted when contact slips past the agreed window.

    nn8nZCZoho CRMSSlack
  4. 4

    Book and confirm the site visit

    Buyers pick a gallery slot on WhatsApp, receive reminders with the location pin and reschedule buttons, and check in by QR code on arrival, which also confirms any channel partner attribution.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  5. 5

    Follow up and learn

    The executive confirms an AI summary of the visit, selected follow-up content goes out, and dashboards show response time, visit show-up and visit-to-booking conversion by source, campaign, partner and executive.

    ACAnthropic ClaudeMPMicrosoft Power BIGAGoogle Analytics 4

  6. People decide

    Sales executives own every qualified conversation and every price, offer or possession-date answer, using the approved price sheet. The sales manager reviews response breaches daily, the partner manager decides attribution conflicts, and marketing and legal approve templates, ad copy and RERA details before launch.

A clear delivery rhythm

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 1

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We walk the journey with pre-sales, sales, CRM, finance, legal, leasing or site teams, map where leads, documents, approvals and site information stall, and review what the CRM, ERP, portals and site apps can expose. We also review consent wording, partner policies, ad approval practice and the RERA details for each project.

  2. 2

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design conversation flows, templates, routing and approval rules, document templates and data flows. Price, legal and safety content is written or approved by your team, and every message type is mapped to its consent basis and channel rules.

  3. 3

    2–4 weeks

    Build

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against test data, set up the consent log, partner and buyer portals, staff queues and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

  4. 4

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test with sales, CRM, finance and site users, run scripted edge cases such as duplicate partner claims, a demand before a registered agreement, a discount request outside the band and a serious site incident, fix what fails and launch on one project, center or site first.

  5. 5

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor failed messages, template quality ratings, response times, approval delays and AI accuracy, review KPIs with your owners every month, and change templates, rules and prompts only through an approved change process.

First pilot: Four-week lead-to-site-visit pilot on one project

Start with one project and its main lead sources: leads are deduplicated, answered with approved content and the RERA number, qualified and assigned with response-time alerts, and visits are booked, reminded and checked in on WhatsApp. We compare response time and visit show-up with the weeks before in your CRM, and track visit-to-booking as bookings follow. Contractors can start with daily site reports instead.

  • One project with portal, Meta or Google and website lead sources connected to the CRM
  • Approved WhatsApp templates and a qualification Flow carrying the RERA registration number
  • Assignment rules, response-time alerts and a named sales manager for escalations
  • Site visit booking, reminders and gallery QR check-in
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of response time and visit show-up, with visit-to-booking tracked after the pilot

Know whether it is working

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Speed to first contact
Median time from lead creation in any source to the first meaningful contact by automation or an executive, by source and for staffed and unstaffed hours.
Lead-to-site-visit conversion
Share of qualified leads in a period that complete a site or video visit, by project, source, partner and executive.
Visit-to-booking conversion
Share of completed visits that lead to a booking within an agreed window, from CRM records.
Partner registration conflict rate
Share of channel partner registrations flagged as duplicates or conflicts, with the median time to a recorded decision.
